transcript.text: Thank you all for joining this curriculum review session. As you know, we're considering a no-cost pilot of an adaptive writing platform for the fall term. The draft proposal has some gaps I need addressed before I can approve it — specifically around the participating grade, data settings, teacher support, and family orientation. I'd like to hear your operational findings so we can shape this pilot properly. Could each of you share what you've found from your respective areas?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I observed the platform in two seventh-grade classrooms, and I found that the useful feedback depended on a six-week cycle with one coached teacher-planning session each week. I recorded this in my coaching notes, but I should note those notes haven't been attached to the draft proposal.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I finished reviewing the vendor's pilot agreement yesterday — after the proposal was circulated. Two key findings: student accounts must operate in local-only mode, and identifiable writing data may be retained for exactly 30 days. These data settings are critical for the proposal and weren't available when it was first shared.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I completed a family-access review and found that participating families need the orientation materials and live session offered in English, Spanish, and Somali. Our family liaison has not yet added those language arrangements to the proposal, so that gap still needs to be filled before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Weekly coached teacher-planning session for the full six-week pilot cycle, per coaching notes.
Student accounts to operate in local-only mode with identifiable writing data retained for exactly 30 days, per vendor pilot agreement.
Orientation materials and live session to be offered in English, Spanish, and Somali before pilot launch.
Attach Mr. Bennett's coaching notes, incorporate Ms. Torres's data settings, and add the family liaison's language arrangements to finalize the proposal.
